Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The failing test `testAddNaN` in the `ComplexTest` class of Apache Commons Math is testing the `add` method of the `Complex` class when one of the operands is a `NaN` value. The test first adds `Complex.NaN` to a `Complex` instance, then adds a new `Complex` instance with a `NaN` value to the original `Complex` instance.

The current bug report mentions that the `Complex` class handles `NaN` values differently in `add` and `subtract` methods, although the Javadoc contracts are the same. The Javadoc specifies that if either the calling `Complex` or the passed `Complex` has a `NaN` value in either part, `Complex.NaN` should be returned. 

Looking at the code snippet of the `add` method in the `Complex` class, it simply adds the real and imaginary parts of two `Complex` instances without explicitly handling the case when one of them is `NaN`.

Based on the failure observed in the test and the discrepancy in handling `NaN` values, it is likely that the `add` method in the `Complex` class does not properly handle `NaN` values as specified in the Javadoc. This could lead to unexpected behavior when adding `NaN` values.

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this issue.
The potential fix for this issue would be to modify the `Complex.add` method in the `Complex` class to properly handle `NaN` values according to the Javadoc contract. 

The method that needs to be fixed is:
```
org.apache.commons.math.complex.Complex.add(org.apache.commons.math.complex.Complex)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
